intro: Lesson 91: Revision: photosynthesis and human nutrition. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: In the starch test on a leaf, why is the leaf boiled in ethanol?
questions.a: B) To remove chlorophyll. Removing the green chlorophyll lets the iodine colour be seen.

questions.q: Name the enzyme that digests lipids.
The factor in shortest supply is the...
Big question: where does the energy in your breakfast originally come from?
questions.a: Light from the Sun, captured by plants in photosynthesis.

questions.q: Describe how to test a leaf for starch.
questions.a: Boil in water to kill and soften (1); in ethanol (in a hot water bath, no flame) to remove chlorophyll (1); rinse in water (1); add iodine: blue-black shows starch (1).
questions.model: Four steps, four marks: boil in water, warm in ethanol in a water bath, rinse, add iodine and look for blue-black.

questions.q: State the function of fibre in the diet.
questions.a: Helps food move through the gut by peristalsis (prevents constipation).
Bile emulsifies fat into small droplets (1), giving a larger surface area for lipase (1).

questions.q: Explain how a leaf is adapted for photosynthesis. Portal response box.
questions.a: Large surface area (1); thin, short diffusion distance (1); many chloroplasts in palisade layer near the top (1); stomata let CO₂ in (1); air spaces in spongy layer (1); veins (xylem) bring water (1).
questions.model: Teacher plans with a feature-reason table: 'Broad and flat: large surface area to absorb light.'

questions.q: A variegated leaf (green and white) is tested for starch. Only the green parts turn blue-black. Explain.
questions.a: Only green parts have chlorophyll (1); chlorophyll absorbs light for photosynthesis (1); so only they made glucose stored as starch (1).

questions.q: Explain why a pregnant woman needs more iron and calcium.
questions.a: Iron for extra haemoglobin for her and the fetus (1); calcium for the fetus's bones and teeth (1).
